title: Parallel Non-Integer Multiple-Cell-Height Node Remapping
problem: Timing-aware node remapping for VLSI circuits with non-integer multiple-cell-height (NIMCH) standard cells suffers from computational overhead due to exhaustive enumeration of all node-to-gate mapping combinations, limiting scalability for large designs.
motivation: Growing circuit complexity with NIMCH cells makes rapid timing closure essential for physical design; existing sequential approaches are too slow for large-scale applications.
method: Proposes two parallel remapping schemes: (1) parallel longest-path-first scheme that prioritizes timing-critical nodes and enables GPU/multicore execution, and (2) iterative minimum-slack-first scheme that also prioritizes timing-critical paths. Both schemes reduce enumeration space by focusing optimization on critical paths rather than exhaustive search.
key_novelty: First parallel NIMCH node remapping flow achieving 5.58× runtime speedup while preserving placement quality through timing-criticality prioritization.
contributions: Parallel longest-path-first scheme enabling concurrent remapping execution
5.58× average runtime speedup over state-of-the-art while maintaining placement quality
limitations: Evaluation on specific VLSI circuits; generalization to different cell libraries not thoroughly explored; area overhead of parallelization not detailed.
